# <type>(<scope>): <subject>
# |<----  Using a Maximum Of 50 Characters  ---->|


# Conventional Commits types:
#   feat   - new user-visible feature  (SemVer MINOR)
#   fix    - bug fix                   (SemVer PATCH)
#   perf   - performance fix           (SemVer PATCH)
#   docs   - documentation only
#   style  - formatting, no logic change
#   refactor - restructure, no behavior change
#   test   - tests only
#   build  - build system or dependencies
#   ci     - CI/CD configuration
#   chore  - maintenance, tooling, config
#   revert - undo a previous commit
#   feat!: / fix!: - breaking change (SemVer MAJOR) - add BREAKING CHANGE footer


# Explain *why* this change was made. The body should provide
# context that the subject line cannot. Wrap at 72 characters.
# Use the imperative mood ("fix bug" not "fixed bug" or "fixes bug").
#
# Blank line separates subject from body.
# Blank line separates body from footers.


# --- Footers ---
# BREAKING CHANGE: <description of incompatible change>
# Closes #<issue-number>
# Refs #<issue-number>
#
# Footers go after a blank line. Each footer is a single line.
# Use GitHub keywords (Closes, Fixes, Resolves) to auto-close issues.
